name: Core Network Intrusion
description: A state-linked actor establishes persistent access in core routing and provisioning systems, positioning to intercept traffic and survive eviction attempts.
asset: Core routing, provisioning, and lawful-intercept systems
assumptions: Detection is assumed to come from external notification; dwell time exceeds six months.
Primary loss covers multi-quarter eviction, rebuild, and outside forensics.
Secondary loss covers regulatory proceedings and national-security reporting obligations.

name: DDoS Against Subscriber Infrastructure
description: Volumetric attacks against DNS, CGNAT, and edge routers degrade service for whole towns until upstream scrubbing absorbs the traffic.
assumptions: Only attacks producing subscriber-visible degradation count as loss events.
Primary loss covers mitigation capacity, overtime, and outage credits.
Secondary loss covers churn in competitive service areas and PUC complaints.

name: Subscriber Billing Data Breach
description: An intrusion into billing and CRM systems exposes subscriber names, addresses, call records, and partial payment data.
assumptions: CPNI protections make call-record exposure a regulatory event regardless of misuse.
Primary loss covers forensics, notification, and FCC-mandated remediation.
Secondary loss covers FCC enforcement, class actions, and churn.

name: SIM-Swap Fraud Through Store Channels
description: Fraudsters socially engineer or bribe retail and support staff to execute unauthorized SIM swaps used to defeat customers' bank MFA.
threat: SIM-swap fraud rings targeting store staff
effect: Customer account takeovers via hijacked numbers
assumptions: The carrier's direct loss is remediation and goodwill; victims' bank losses arrive as claims.
Attempts track subscriber count and dark-web demand for target numbers.
Secondary loss covers FCC scrutiny and liability claims from downstream fraud.

name: Ransomware in Business Support Systems
description: Ransomware encrypts OSS/BSS servers — provisioning, billing, and support tooling — leaving the network running but unmanageable.
assumptions: Subscriber traffic keeps flowing; the loss is management-plane paralysis and billing delay.
New activations and truck rolls halt during the outage window.
Secondary loss covers delayed revenue recognition and regulatory reporting.
